text_post: RE: Movie to be made about AVFM Great news, remember the 2 golden rules of getting your story across.  Verifiable Facts only, and use the least favourable numbers you can find, therefore anyone investigating your claims will see you have embellished none of it.  there are 3 groups out there, those on your side, those against you and those in between. the latter is your target. dont try and denounce feminism, just state your goals, state your claims, state your evidence and the truth will out. very positive about this, just be very careful that they dont edit it heavily and make you look stupid.

author: Usagi Yojimbo
text_post: RE: Movie to be made about AVFM Be very, very careful with this, folks. Through my father and the nature of his job, I have a very strong distrust of the press and media.  All too often the media have an angle they wish to play, and will twist and edit whatever one says to satisfy getting their angle made.  I have seen it done, as have a lot of us; news spun to favor the feminist point of view, movies warped from the original story, and so on.  It could very well lead to a witch hunt on you. Force the issue to make sure true objectivity is maintained, and make them stay true to the course.  Make sure to control the narrative in the movie to be objective as possible, (I believe Rowling made sure she had control of the Harry Potter movies so they would hold as true to the novels as possible in the movie deal.)  If it is within your power, make sure they show you their release cut prior to release to make sure it is held true to the cause. Don't get me wrong, this would be the best opportunity to get the news out, and maybe put a few more on the red pill path.   But prior experience makes me want to keep a jaded eye out for something that could possibly hurt us.   Watch your backs.

author: Ortho Stice
text_post: RE: Movie to be made about AVFM I would echo the voices counseling caution. Even media types who seem friendly can have agendas they won't tell you about. I would throw in three things: 1. Have documentation for any factual claim you make. Make sure the producers have it before your part in the film is done. 2. Don't let them manipulate you during the interview. Just ask Newt Gingrich's mom, Sarah Palin, or Belladonna (the porn star) how that goes. They have techniques to get you upset and angry that have been honed over years. 3. Stay on message. As an intelligent non-politician, you will be tempted to answer questions with statements that actually, you know, answer the question. Don't do it. Every question is an opportunity for you to say what you want to say, regardless of what's asked. If you're very skilled, you can make it seem like you're answering the question, but that's not really necessary. (I'm not exaggerating. This is what politicians do, and if it didn't work, they wouldn't do it.)
